exposure: Fetal tumors evaluated by ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
Ultrasound and MRI characteristics (tumor morphology, compromise of surrounding structures, brain alterations)
outcome: Morbidity (survival with minor or serious illness)
Long-term outcome (healthy, minor illness, serious illness)
cohort: The study included 68 pregnancies with prenatally diagnosed fetal tumors at a single center between 1998 and 2018.
finding: The study found a high rate of survivors with serious long-term illness among fetuses with prenatal tumor diagnoses, and MRI was specifically helpful for risk stratification in fetal teratomas and delivery planning in head and neck tumors.
mod_finding: MRI was found to be superior to ultrasound for delivery planning in head and neck tumors, implying its relevance for mode of birth considerations.
